newsitem.title: USA: Reuters journalist released on bail from U.S. jail.
newsitem.headline: Reuters journalist released on bail from U.S. jail.

text.p: A Reuters journalist was released on bail from a Washington, D.C., jail on Tuesday, a day after she was arrested at the White House while covering the visit of Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.
Wafa Amr, 35, was released on $10,000 bond after her attorneys said she would return to Iowa to face a warrant for her arrest dating from 1982, when she was a college student.
Iowa prosecutors said Amr had been charged in 1982 with second degree theft based on $3,021 in bad checks. She paid the money back the same year, they said.
The warrant for Amr's arrest was issued after she did not appear for a final hearing on the case in August, 1982, said David Tiffany, assistant prosecutor in Johnson County, Iowa.
"I thought this matter had been taken care of in 1982 before I left Iowa," Amr said after her release on Tuesday evening.

Amr, a Reuters staff correspondent in Jerusalem since 1993, was detained by the U.S. Secret Service on Monday at a White House gate as she arrived to cover Arafat's meeting with President Bill Clinton.
She was taken to a holding room and questioned for several hours, led away in handcuffs and spent the night in jail.

Amr is a Palestinian who carries a Jordanian passport. She has written extensively about Arafat and the Middle East peace process, and has travelled to the United States several times to cover the peace process. She covered the signing of a peace accord by Arafat and the late Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin in September, 1995 at the White House.
"We are continuing to provide legal counsel and assistance to our correspondent in bringing this matter to a final resolution," Reuters spokesman Robert Crooke said.
